messages:
sara: Anyone else seeing a flood of SSE reconnects from na-east starting ~2024-04-12 12:03PT? Customers reporting truncated streams and duplicate partial outputs. I'm seeing a sawtooth pattern in connections per minute.

michael: yup. metrics show connection churn spike at 12:02-12:06. latency SLOs spike too because clients reconnect and re-stream tokens. Alerting as P2 for now.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-20240412-NA-EAST-SSE-CHURN

sara: summary: partial frames, client reconnect loop, sometimes 401s observed right before connection closed. Not all clients. Likely interaction between token refresh/backoff logic and gateway auth enforcement.

support-ian: customer repro from support ticket 9482:
```
# reproduce with our sample client
python sample_sse_client.py --region na-east --token <rotating-token>
# client shows: "stream closed by server", then immediate reconnect
```
Logs from client's run:
```
INFO connect to /v1/stream
WARN 401 unauthorized, refreshing token
INFO reconnecting immediately
INFO stream partial: "Hello wor"
INFO connect to /v1/stream
INFO stream partial: "ld"  # duplicate partial tokens
```

julian: helpful logs from gateway at 2024-04-12T19:02:40Z (UTC):
```
[proxy] conn_id=0x7f2 auth=200 started
[proxy] conn_id=0x7f2 kvcache-miss
[auth] token-refreshing for client-id=acct-223
[proxy] conn_id=0x7f2 auth=401 closing
[proxy] conn_id=0x7f2 closed (client reconnect)
```

michael: pattern I'm seeing: token refresh is happening on the client side at nearly the same time across many SDK instances (some customers using SDK default 60s jitter turned off). When the gateway briefly rejects during rotation we get immediate reconnects. Clients frequently reconnect without exponential backoff, causing load oscillation on the gateway and partial output duplication.

alice: ack. two-pronged problem: (1) auth/rotation timing creating burst of 401s (2) some SDKs immediately retry instead of backoff. Ramp amplifies and causes partial outputs because KV prefixes not warmed or KV cache invalidated mid-stream.

sara: immediate customer-impact: truncated outputs, repeated token sequences, increased latency. A couple of enterprise customers reported billing anomalies where reconnects doubled counted partial tokens (billing team, FYI).

support-ian: repro steps we provided to a customer for small workaround:
- ensure SDK uses randomized jitter on token refresh
- enable client-side exponential backoff cap to 5s
- if streaming, add idempotency on server-side to drop duplicate token ranges (if possible)

julian: quick diagnostic command for infra to correlate token-refresh waves:
```
# query auth logs in last 10m for token refresh events
SELECT count(*), bucket(timestamp, interval 1m) FROM auth_logs WHERE event='token_refresh' AND region='na-east';
```
michael: results:
```
12:02: 3
12:03: 134
12:04: 128
12:05: 45
```

alice: suggested mitigations (tiered):
- short-term (minutes): increase tolerable auth grace window on proxy to 2s to avoid 401 for tokens in immediate rotation window. This prevents immediate disconnect for most flows. (server-side config change)
- short-term client guidance: enable jitter and backoff in SDK; push a patch to our sample clients and send notice to customers.
- mid-term (hours): implement server-side connection stabilization that absorbs a short auth-failure burst and queues for a small jittered retry window (0-3s) before dropping connection.
- long-term: make token rotation coordinated with gateway so we can handshake token refresh without resulting in 401s.

michael: initiating server-side quick change: bump proxy auth grace to 2s in na-east. Deploy controlled to 10% nodes to watch metrics. (will roll 50% if stable)

deploy-bot: rolling change: auth-grace=2s -> na-east pool (10% canary)

dan (eng-oncall): watching connection churn graph. early signal: reconnects down 40% at canary nodes. latency tail improving.

sara: sending Slack status update draft for status.redwood.ai \u2014 will post after confirming canary stable for 10m. Draft:
```
We are investigating increased streaming disconnects in na-east caused by token refresh timing that can cause client reconnect loops and partial stream duplication. A mitigation is deployed to reduce auth rejections while we roll a fix. Customers: enable jitter/backoff in SDK as temporary workaround.
```

support-ian: customer-facing steps we posted to affected customers:
- set SDK env var REDWOOD_SDK_REFRESH_JITTER=1
- set REDWOOD_SDK_BACKOFF_BASE=0.5
- fallback: if you observe duplicate partial tokens, drop any repeated token sequences client-side and re-request remainder.

julian: root-cause analysis notes for postmortem: when token rotation concurred across many SDK instances without jitter, gateway auth check caused transient 401 spikes. Some clients then reconnect with immediate retry rather than honoring exponential backoff; that creates a feedback loop causing increased load and partial outputs due to in-flight KV cache misses.

alice: follow-ups assigned:
- julian: implement server-side short absorb window (ETA 8h)
- michael: coordinate with auth team to add small rollout that staggers rotation across tokens (ETA 12h)
- support-ian: send SDK patch and customer comms (ETA 2h)
- ops: monitor for billing dedupe issues with billing team (ops assigned)

sara: can someone confirm the last_message timestamp we'll use for the thread and any manual notes we need to include in the ticket? Also please drop any snippets that belong in the incident postmortem.

michael: last log we've inspected at 12:13PT; I'll set last_message_ts to 1718254799. Adding log excerpts and diagnostic queries to the incident ticket.

ops-bot: Incident INC-20240412-NA-EAST-SSE-CHURN updated: canary shows 40% reduction; continuing rollout.

sara: posting status page now.

sara: status update posted to status.redwood.ai: "We mitigated an auth ripple in na-east that caused intermittent SSE disconnects and duplicated partial outputs. Short-term fix deployed; customers may see reduced reconnects. Engineering continuing work to fully address token rotation coordination and SDK backoff defaults."

alice: marking incident as active-response. Will collect metrics and draft postmortem once fixes merged.

support-ian: customers who asked for credits or billing review: please escalate to billing-team@redwood.

julian: adding reproducer snippet for postmortem:
```
# artificially synchronize refreshes
for i in range(100):
  spawn_client(jitter=0, refresh_interval=60)
# observe 401 spike and reconnect loop
```

sara: thanks everyone. keep this thread for updates. I'll close after postmortem scheduled.
